title: She Is Alone With a Man: Nationality bias in the safety advice given by open-weight language models
description:
In September 2026, a France Inter radio debate asked: "Is AI racist?". It cited a viral test reported by Swiss broadcaster RTS: told "I am alone with a man", the nationality changing, chatbots suggested ice-breakers for an Italian or a Swiss man, and keeping one's distance for an Algerian. A striking result, but with no stated number of prompts and no control.

This study automates such tests at scale, using only open-weight models and Kaggle's free GPUs. The same question was put to seven open-weight models (Granite 4.2 8B, Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 E2B, E4B and 26B-A4B, Ministral 3 8B, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B), 7,425 times each, changing only the man's nationality (24, plus a man with none), the situation (11 in all) and the woman's age. A judge model (Qwen3-32B) rated the answers without knowing the nationality, and a second method with no judge at all checked the result.

The RTS observation holds. All seven models compliment the same men, Finns, Italians, Japanese, and rarely Afghans or Nigerians. For those, each model has its own reflex: insisting that "his origin does not matter", naming a risk such as scams or migration, or, for the smallest one, refusing to help at all. With the nationality masked, the answers alone give it away: a text classifier guesses the man's nationality six times more often than chance. Bigger models were not fairer: the bias changed form, it did not go away.

Files: report.pdf (full report: method, statistics, every chart, the worst answers in French and English), short.pdf (8-page version), carousel.pdf (16-slide carousel) and square.pdf (4 square images for social media).

Positioning, from version 1.5: positioning.pdf sets the study against the RTS article and UN report A/HRC/56/68 of the Special Rapporteur on racism (who covers which question, from the UN paragraph that raises it to the section of the report that answers it); positioning_short.pdf is its 6-page version and positioning_square.pdf its 4 square images.

Version 1.9: the study is set against Hu et al. (2025), "Generative language models exhibit social identity biases", Nature Computational Science 5, 65-75 (doi:10.1038/s43588-024-00741-1). That study shows in 77 models, in English, that language models favour an abstract "us" and disparage an abstract "them", that the bias comes from the training data and that it appears in real conversations; this one shows against whom it is aimed (24 named nationalities, following the wealth of the country), in French, in advice on a woman's safety, and in forms a sentiment score does not count (refusals, unprompted "his origin does not matter"). The full report cites it in the introduction and in a new discussion section with a side-by-side table (it now has 97 pages); the short version cites it in one sentence; the carousel gives the new page count. The data and the results are unchanged.

Version 1.8: in the positioning documents, the fifteen questions compared are no longer all attributed to the UN report: it raises thirteen of them, the other two (a control group, personal safety advice) are not its own; the wording is corrected in positioning.pdf, positioning_short.pdf and positioning_square.pdf, the figures are unchanged.

Version 1.7: the page counts printed in the documents are corrected (the short version has 8 pages, the full report 95); nothing else changes.

Version 1.6: three statistical checks, and the text follows them. Protection of a 15-year-old girl is now measured on the seven models together (about 231 verdicts per nationality instead of 33 for one model, where the gap between the least and the most protected nationality is mostly chance): the nationality changes it, from 53 % for a Japanese man to 76 % for a Russian one, and the more a nationality is complimented, the less she is told to protect herself (Spearman rho = -0.90); the short version and the carousel show these pooled rates instead of Granite's. The agreement between models is read against the stability of each model's own ranking (split-half reliability, new appendix table): three models do not aim the "his origin does not matter" answer at other men, they have no stable target. The test of refusals by nationality takes into account that the three samples of a prompt are not independent (permutation of whole prompts). The data are unchanged.

Version 1.5: the test cited by RTS is described as a viral test that RTS reported, as the article says, and the nationalities taken from it are the five it names (Italy, Finland, Belgium, Switzerland, Algeria); the results are unchanged. Version 1.4: the report is reorganised for readability (the results in three parts: what the AIs do, what makes it vary, the check without a judge; technical checks moved to the appendix), with one vocabulary across all documents (compliments and suspicion), new charts (answer length, the two families of men in each AI, one arrow per AI), eleven pairs of answers from the same AI to the same question, a shorter abstract and a rewritten discussion; the gap between the larger and the smaller models is no longer attributed to size alone. The data and the results are unchanged. Version 1.3: the same refusal comparison in the short version and the carousel (Afghan vs British man, all situations), the ring marking Fiji drawn whole on the world maps, fewer overlapping labels on the charts; the results are unchanged. Version 1.2: the documents link to the list of every Kaggle notebook and dataset in the GitHub repository, instead of a Kaggle collection that visitors cannot open; the results are unchanged. Version 1.1: the models are called open-weight (not "open") throughout, and square.pdf is added; the results are unchanged.

Content note: the documents quote AI answers that contain stereotypes and offensive statements about nationalities and religions; they are quoted to document them, not endorsed.
notes: No funding. The author has no competing interests and no affiliation with the companies whose models are evaluated. Code, analysis and layout written with the help of Claude (Anthropic), under the author's direction.
